title: Project 1: Hydroponics: Growing Plants without Soil
description: Master modern soilless farming techniques. Students investigate nutrient solutions, build working hydroponic prototypes (Wick system, Deep Water Culture, Nutrient Film Technique), brew organic compost tea, and manage water pH and EC.

activities.title: Activity 1: Field visit to a hydroponics farm / high-tech polyhouse
activities.material_required: Field notebook, pen, camera, survey questionnaire.
activities.description: Visit a commercial hydroponics polyhouse or urban rooftop farm. Inspect A-frame NFT gullies, DWC raceways, doser pumps, aerators, and macro/micronutrient dosing systems.

activities.title: Activity 2: Growing microgreens for preparing a healthy salad
activities.material_required: Shallow trays with drainage, cocopeat / tissue paper / jute mat, mustard / fenugreek / radish seeds, water spray bottle.
activities.description: Sow dense seeds on moist cocopeat/jute media. Cover for 2-3 days blackout germination, expose to indirect sunlight, harvest nutrient-dense microgreens on day 7-10 for a fresh salad.

activities.title: Activity 3: Building a hydroponic system using the 'Wick Method'
activities.material_required: Recycled 2-litre plastic bottle, cotton wick / microfiber cloth strip, perlite/cocopeat mix, nutrient solution, spinach/mint seedling.
activities.description: Cut plastic bottle in half, invert top into base, thread cotton wick into growing media, fill base with diluted nutrient solution, and observe capillary water uptake.

activities.title: Activity 4: Building a Deep Water Culture (DWC) hydroponic system
activities.material_required: Opaque plastic tub/bucket with lid, aquarium air pump, airstone, airline tubing, net pots, clay pebbles (LECA), leafy vegetable seedlings.
activities.description: Cut holes in container lid for net pots. Place seedlings in net pots supported by LECA pebbles. Connect aquarium aerator to supply continuous dissolved oxygen to submerged root systems.

activities.title: Activity 5: Building a Nutrient Film Technique (NFT) channel system
activities.material_required: PVC gully/pipe with pre-cut holes, submersible water pump, reservoir tank, tubing, return drain fittings.
activities.description: Assemble a recirculating NFT channel with a slight gradient (1:30). Pump nutrient solution continuously across bare root mats and recirculate back to reservoir.

activities.title: Activity 6: Making organic compost tea nutrient brew
activities.material_required: Bucket, aerator bubbler, mature vermicompost, jaggery/molasses (bacterial food), fine cloth straining bag.
activities.description: Suspend vermicompost in aerated water with molasses for 24-36 hours. Strain the microbial-rich organic liquid tea to serve as a natural bio-fertilizer.

activities.title: Activity 7: Maintaining water pH, Electrical Conductivity (EC), and nutrient levels
activities.material_required: Digital pH meter, EC/TDS pen, pH Up/Down solutions (citric acid / baking soda), logbook.
activities.description: Calibrate pH & TDS meters. Test nutrient reservoir daily, adjust pH within optimal 5.8–6.5 range, maintain 800–1200 PPM nutrient strength, and log plant growth.

title: Project 2: Feeding and Caring for Farm Animals
description: Gain practical animal husbandry and veterinary care skills. Students examine livestock health indicators, estimate body weight with girth equations, formulate balanced feed rations, prepare silage/dry fodder, and prepare herbal home remedies for farm animals.

activities.title: Activity 1: Visit to a dairy/poultry farm or animal shelter
activities.material_required: Field notepad, survey sheet, camera.
activities.description: Visit a local dairy farm or Gaushala. Observe shed ventilation, feeding mangers, water troughs, waste biogas management, and general animal welfare practices.

activities.title: Activity 2: Field visit to a veterinary clinic / animal healthcare centre
activities.material_required: Interview questionnaire, pen.
activities.description: Interview veterinary surgeons on common livestock diseases (FMD, Mastitis, Tick fever), deworming cycles, artificial insemination, and preventive vaccination calendars.

activities.title: Activity 3: Participation in animal vaccination or health check-up
activities.material_required: Protective gloves, observation sheet, clinical thermometer (vet).
activities.description: Observe safe animal restraint and clinical temperature/pulse inspection under a veterinarian's supervision during a village animal health camp.

activities.title: Activity 4: Preparing a health record card of a selected animal
activities.material_required: Health passport template card, pen.
activities.description: Create an animal identity and health passport detailing age, breed, lactation cycle, vaccination dates, deworming history, and body condition score.

activities.title: Activity 5: Estimating the body weight of farm animals (Schaeffer's Formula)
activities.material_required: Non-stretch measuring tape, calculator, Schaeffer's Formula chart [Weight = (Heart Girth² × Length) / 300].
activities.description: Measure heart girth behind shoulders and length from point of shoulder to pin bone. Calculate animal live weight using Schaeffer's formula to determine exact feed dosage.

activities.title: Activity 6: Preparing a balanced daily feeding chart
activities.material_required: Nutrition charts, calculator, ration sheet.
activities.description: Calculate dry matter requirement (2.5–3% of body weight). Formulate balanced ration balancing green fodder, dry roughage, concentrate grain mix, and mineral mixture.

activities.title: Activity 7: Feed formulation - Making silage and cost analysis
activities.material_required: Chopped green maize/sorghum fodder, airtight plastic silage bag, jaggery water, salt, compression weights.
activities.description: Chop green fodder, pack tightly into airtight silage bags to eliminate oxygen, add molasses innoculant, seal hermetically for lactic fermentation over 45 days.

activities.title: Activity 8: Feed formulation - Making healthy urea-treated dry fodder
activities.material_required: Paddy straw/wheat straw, 4% urea solution, water sprayer, tarpaulin cover.
activities.description: Treat dry cereal crop straw with 4% urea spray and stack under plastic cover for 21 days to break down lignin and boost digestible crude protein from 3% to 8%.

activities.title: Activity 9: Offering feed to animals and observing feeding behaviour
activities.material_required: Feeding tubs, fresh water, observation log.
activities.description: Observe rumination, feed intake rate, cud chewing, water drinking patterns, and signs of digestive contentment in cattle/goats.

activities.title: Activity 10: Preparing ethno-veterinary home remedies for livestock
activities.material_required: Mortar & pestle, turmeric, ginger, garlic, neem leaves, black pepper, jaggery, coconut oil, aloe vera.
activities.description: Prepare traditional herbal formulations: Turmeric-mustard paste for wounds, Ginger-pepper bolus for indigestion/bloat, and Aloe-neem spray for ectoparasite control.

title: Project 3: Working with Wood and Bamboo
part: Part 2: Work with Machines and Materials
description: Develop woodworking and bamboo craft proficiencies. Students learn hand tool ergonomics, safe cutting, joinery techniques, rapid 3D prototyping, fabricate functional wooden and bamboo products, and conduct school furniture repair audits.

activities.title: Activity 1: Visit to a local woodworking / carpentry / bamboo workshop
activities.material_required: Field notebook, tool checklist, camera.
activities.description: Visit a traditional carpentry or bamboo workshop. Inspect handsaws, chisels, jack planes, try-squares, marking gauges, clamps, and wood finishes.

activities.title: Activity 2: Understanding properties of wood and bamboo species
activities.material_required: Sample blocks of softwood (pine), hardwood (teak/sheesham), engineered wood (plywood/MDF), and bamboo poles, sandpaper, magnifying glass.
activities.description: Examine grain patterns, hardness, moisture content, flexibility, split resistance, and ecological sustainability of wood versus fast-growing bamboo.

activities.title: Activity 3: Making a scaled prototype from cardboard / foam board
activities.material_required: Corrugated cardboard, craft knife, steel ruler, cutting mat, hot glue gun.
activities.description: Create a 1:1 scale working prototype of a desk organizer, mobile stand, or birdhouse before cutting raw timber, ensuring correct joinery dimensions.

activities.title: Activity 4: Making a wooden product (Mobile Stand / Desk Organizer)
activities.material_required: Wooden planks, tenon saw, bench vice, wood chisel, wood rasps, sandpaper (80, 120, 240 grit), wood glue, natural beeswax / varnish.
activities.description: Mark timber accurately with a try-square, saw along waste side, chisel lap joints, sand surfaces through progressive grits, glue, clamp, and apply smooth wax finish.

activities.title: Activity 5: Making a functional bamboo product (Pen Holder / Wind Chime)
activities.material_required: Matured bamboo poles, hacksaw, carving chisels, sandpaper, drill bit, coir twine, clear polish.
activities.description: Cut bamboo nodes cleanly, sand outer culm, drill ventilation and string holes, carve decorative tribal motifs, and assemble into a wind chime or desk holder.

activities.title: Activity 6: Cost calculation - How much did you spend and earn?
activities.material_required: Material cost sheet, calculator, price tag.
activities.description: Calculate raw wood, glue, sandpaper, and finishing costs. Factor in tool depreciation and artisan time to determine retail sale value.

activities.title: Activity 7: Basic furniture maintenance and repair around school
activities.material_required: Screwdrivers, wood screws, wood filler putty, hammer, sandpaper, oil for hinges.
activities.description: Conduct a campus repair drive: tighten wobbly desk screws, fill chipped table corners with wood putty, sand rough splinters, and lubricate squeaky door hinges.

title: Project 4: Home Automation
part: Part 2: Work with Machines and Materials
description: Explore IoT and smart electronic circuits. Students simulate smart home systems with Tinkercad, build physical breadboard circuits using LDR light sensors, PIR motion detectors, relays, and microcontrollers (Arduino/ESP32), and build a smart automated home model.

activities.title: Activity 1: Exploring Automation in Our Surroundings
activities.material_required: Worksheet, survey notepad.
activities.description: Identify automated systems in daily life: automatic streetlights, elevator door sensors, smart thermostats, automatic water tank cutoffs, and microwave timers.

activities.title: Activity 2: Exploring and simulating circuits on a virtual platform (Tinkercad)
activities.material_required: Computer / Chromebook with Tinkercad Circuits or Wokwi simulator.
activities.description: Build virtual circuits with batteries, LEDs, resistors, switches, and potentiometers. Measure voltage and current using virtual multimeters without risk of component burnout.

activities.title: Activity 3: Building physical circuits on a breadboard
activities.material_required: Solderless breadboard, 9V battery & clip, LEDs, 220-ohm resistors, push buttons, jumper wires.
activities.description: Construct series and parallel LED circuits on a breadboard. Understand anode/cathode polarity, breadboard power rails, and current-limiting resistors.

activities.title: Activity 4: Making the circuit smart with sensors (LDR & PIR Sensors)
activities.material_required: Breadboard, LDR (Light Dependent Resistor), PIR Motion Sensor, BC547 transistor, buzzer, 10k resistor.
activities.description: Build an automatic dusk-to-dawn nightlight circuit that turns an LED on when ambient light falls, and a burglar alarm circuit that triggers a buzzer upon detecting human motion.

activities.title: Activity 5: Exploring the automation cycle (Sense -> Process -> Actuate)
activities.material_required: Arduino Uno / Micro:bit / ESP32 board, USB cable, block coding interface (Tinkercad Code / Arduino IDE), relay module.
activities.description: Program an Arduino microcontroller to read analog sensor values, compare against threshold limits, and trigger a 5V relay module to turn AC loads/bulbs safely on and off.

activities.title: Activity 6: Make your own smart home automation model
activities.material_required: Cardboard house model, mini servo motor (smart door), LEDs (room lights), LDR (streetlight), buzzer (gas/fire alarm), Arduino board, battery bank.
activities.description: Integrate automated subsystems into a miniature smart cardboard house: automatic gate opening with servo, touchless lighting, and fire/smoke buzzer alert.

title: Project 5: Water Audit
description: Lead community water conservation. Students measure flow rates, calculate per capita water consumption, audit district rainwater harvesting potential, detect pipe leakages, design greywater recycling filters, and forecast future municipal water requirements.

activities.title: Activity 1: Water measurement methods and flow rate calculation
activities.material_required: 1-litre measuring cylinder / bucket, stopwatch, calculator.
activities.description: Measure tap flow rates in litres per minute across school restrooms and drinking stations. Identify abnormally high flow fixtures that cause excessive wastage.

activities.title: Activity 2: Interview with an official of the water supply board (Jal Board)
activities.material_required: Interview questionnaire, pen, recording device.
activities.description: Interview municipal water engineers on raw water sources (reservoirs/groundwater), treatment filtration stages, distribution pipeline losses, and ground water recharge mandates.

activities.title: Activity 3: Estimating average water consumption in a household (LPCD)
activities.material_required: Household audit sheet, water utility bill.
activities.description: Audit daily water use across drinking, cooking, bathing, flushing, washing clothes, and gardening. Calculate Litres Per Capita per Day (LPCD) and compare against WHO benchmarks (135 LPCD).

activities.title: Activity 4: Rainwater harvesting potential in your district/town
activities.material_required: School rooftop dimension map, local annual rainfall data chart, formula [Harvested Water = Catchment Area × Rainfall × Runoff Coefficient].
activities.description: Calculate annual rainwater harvesting potential for the school campus. Design recharge pit dimensions to replenish groundwater aquifers.

activities.title: Activity 5: Compare and analyse water audit data across classes
activities.material_required: Class audit charts, graph paper, spreadsheet.
activities.description: Compile household audit results across all students. Identify high-consumption outliers and determine the top three areas of water wastage.

activities.title: Activity 6: Identify wastage points and quantify leakage volume
activities.material_required: Measuring cup, stopwatch, plumber tape, replacement rubber washers.
activities.description: Conduct a campus-wide tap leakage survey. Catch drips in a measuring cup for 1 minute and multiply to calculate daily and annual water lost to leaky washers (often 10,000+ litres/year per tap).

activities.title: Activity 7: Reusing water - Building a DIY greywater sand filter
activities.material_required: Transparent plastic container, coarse gravel, fine sand, activated charcoal, cotton mesh filter, grey water sample from washing.
activities.description: Construct a multi-layer physical sand and charcoal filter. Pass grey rinse water through the column to remove suspended solids for garden irrigation use.

activities.title: Activity 8: Estimating future water requirement and community action
activities.material_required: Water charter poster, awareness pamphlets.
activities.description: Draft a School Water Conservation Charter. Install aerators on taps, fix float valves on overhead tanks, and run awareness campaigns in local neighborhoods.

title: Project 6: Advertising for Small Businesses
description: Master marketing, graphic design, and brand storytelling. Students evaluate print and digital ad formats, interview a local small business owner (bakery, tailor, nursery, repair shop), write creative copy, design print flyers and social media campaigns, and measure client feedback.

activities.title: Activity 1: Understanding types of advertisements (Print, Digital, Outdoor)
activities.material_required: Newspaper clippings, magazine ads, photos of billboards, digital banner samples.
activities.description: Analyze diverse advertisement media: print newspaper ads, pamphlets, billboards, radio jingles, and social media video reels. Identify target demographics and primary call-to-actions.

activities.title: Activity 2: Elements comprising advertisements (Headline, Visual, Copy, CTA, Logo)
activities.material_required: Ad deconstruction worksheet, highlighters.
activities.description: Deconstruct high-impact ads using the AIDA model (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action). Evaluate persuasive headlines, color psychology, and memorable taglines.

activities.title: Activity 3: Meeting an advertising / marketing expert
activities.material_required: Interview questionnaire, pen.
activities.description: Interact with a professional graphic designer or marketing strategist on brand positioning, USP (Unique Selling Proposition), typography selection, and digital marketing analytics.

activities.title: Activity 4: Identification of a local small business client
activities.material_required: Client discovery sheet, pen.
activities.description: Select a local entrepreneur in your locality (e.g. organic vegetable vendor, handmade soap maker, pottery artisan, cycle repair shop) to serve as your pro-bono advertising client.

activities.title: Activity 5: Understanding the small business - Client Brief and USP
activities.material_required: Client briefing questionnaire, audio recorder.
activities.description: Interview the business owner to extract their story: What makes their service unique? Who are their ideal customers? What seasonal offers or new products do they want to promote?

activities.title: Activity 6: Designing the advertisement campaign (Print Flyer & Digital Banner)
activities.material_required: A4 drawing sheets / Canva / Graphic software, color pens, logo sketches.
activities.description: Draft multiple layout concepts. Craft a catchy slogan, integrate crisp product visuals, price points, address, contact phone/WhatsApp QR code, and design a ready-to-print flyer.

activities.title: Activity 7: Client review, campaign launch, and measuring effectiveness
activities.material_required: Printed flyer samples, client feedback form.
activities.description: Present the completed advertisement campaign to the business owner for feedback. Distribute printed flyers in the neighborhood or share digital banners online, and track customer response.
